newsitem.title: GERMANY: German coffee consumers resigned to price strength.
newsitem.headline: German coffee consumers resigned to price strength.

text.p: German coffee roasters are expecting further price strength in the raw materials market and have reduced buying to replacement cover, traders said on Monday.
"Exaggerated tightness fears seen over the last few weeks have calmed down but so has consumer interest for shipment after February," one said.
"Spot and afloat coffees are being sought, which tells me that the industry's cover is really thin," he added.
"Nevertheless there is no panic...I believe roasters will continue to accompany the market with spot purchases and look into retail price rises."
New York arabicas may be dipping short-term during corrective moves but March was seen ready to test 145/150 cents/lb afterwards, having ended at 139.40 on Friday.
The market should remain firm over the next few weeks although the March/May spread was seen coming under pressure as funds were expected to roll March positions into May.
With the dollar firm and futures headed higher, roasters needed higher earnings and also had enough reasons to justify retail hikes, traders said.
There was talk German, French and Scandinavian price rises were in the pipeline but no names were coming forward.
In the physical market, East African, Brazilian and Colombian arabica prices were considered too high so that Central American sales were the key feature.
Brazils were offered at $157 fob ex-origin, up $3 on the week, with Colombians at $172 fob, up $2. Guatemalan HB was off $1 at $160 fob and Vietnam G-2 robustas were off $6 at $66 cif.
